question: Where do saved native and actual six-load FE fields violate pointwise traction equilibrium?
hypotheses: Unresolved traction jumps concentrate in curve-incident patches
Important equilibrium defects also lie in ordinary wall or bulk regions
A small local residual correction cannot by itself explain the retained-model disagreement
selection: At most 512 uniformly sampled faces per geometry-defined stratum, selected before reading stress values, fixed seed 20261026; a second seed can test sampling stability after reading this run
measurement: h_F times surface integral of six-load traction Gram; normalize trace by each route's complete stiffness tensor and divide by six. Expand sampled stratum sums by population/sample count. No rigorous error constant or sampling confidence interval is asserted.
quadrature: Positive 9 and 16 point triangle rules; check per-face Gram stability before trusting group rankings
controls: Affine and exact quadratic fields have zero jump; continuous kink is detected; orientation reversal preserves Gram; tangential stress gives zero free-wall traction; generic stress gives nonzero traction
limits: Saved-field diagnostic only, 180 seconds and 8 GiB, one numerical thread, no mesh/field/reference changes or new FE solve
next_decision: Read group shares, periodic mismatches and quadrature sensitivity before selecting another diagnostic. No allocation or stiffness claim follows from residual magnitude alone.
